chunks: Zurarah asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام.

About a man who goes out with a group on a journey that he intends, and the prayer time enters for him after he has left the village by two farsakhs, so they pray, and some of them turn back for a need, and it is not decreed for them to continue the departure. What should he do regarding the prayer that he had prayed as two rakʿahs?
He عليه السلام said: “His prayer is complete, and he does not repeat it.”

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rakʿahs, referring to the shortened traveler’s prayer
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel or journey that establishes the context for the ruling
key_terms.فَرْسَخَيْنِ: two farsakhs, the travel distance mentioned in the case
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he repeats; here, repetition is negated

ai.seo_question: If someone prays qasr during travel and then the journey is canceled, must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about salat during travel. If a traveler has already reached the distance at which shortened prayer applies and prays two rakʿahs, then later the journey is interrupted and they do not proceed, that prayer remains valid and does not need to be repeated.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1271 – Zurarah asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as)

about a man who sets out with a group of people for a journey that he intends to complete. The time for prayer enters while they have already departed from the village by a distance of two farsakhs (approximately six miles) and they perform their prayers (as two units). Some of them then turn back for a specific need, and they are unable to continue their journey. What should be done about the prayer that was performed as two units?
Imam (as) said: "His prayer is complete and he does not need to repeat it”.
